clue.text: Demand silence? Well, I never!

parts.note: 'go' in its colloquial sense of 'say', so to demand silence is to go 'sh'
SH is the hushing sound used to demand silence

explanation.surface: Someone shushes a noisy room and a startled onlooker exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Demand silence?' as 'go "sh"', with 'go' meaning 'say'; the question mark flags that loose reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, interchangeable in speech.

clue.text: Writing material Greek character stuffed inside jar

indicators.note: the Greek letter is packed into the word for jar

parts.note: to jar is to grate, as on the nerves
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek letter written on a scrap stuffed into a jar.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphite is the carbon used as the lead in pencils.

clue.text: Dark gold turned-up hat

parts.note: sombre means dark

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up reverses the letters

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Describing a dark, gold-trimmed hat with a turned-up brim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned-up' makes RO of OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a wide-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Current article on Belgian author

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
'an' is the indefinite article
a Fleming is a Flemish-speaking native of Belgium

explanation.surface: A news item about the current state of a Belgian writer's affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places the pieces one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: The creator of James Bond was a British novelist, an example of a writer.

clue.text: Put on suit

definitions.meaning: to put on, as with paint or cream on a surface
to suit is to be relevant, as a rule that holds in a case

explanation.definitionFit: Apply means to spread on a surface, and also to be relevant or fitting.

clue.text: Dreadfully unfair about almost inordinate admiration relating to Cable

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the shortened word
done dreadfully, so the letters of unfair are jumbled
almost all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a cult is excessive devotion to a person or thing

explanation.surface: Suggests a protest that adoration of a politician named Cable is dreadfully unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cable' looks like Vince Cable, a British politician, which explains the capital; really it is the cable that hauls the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A funicular railway is one hauled up a slope by cable.

clue.text: Excessively upset? Only at Brexit!

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether people are overly upset about Brexit alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Exorbitantly means to an unreasonable degree, beyond bounds.

clue.text: Whole piece of meat cat nibbled around

indicators.note: turned around, so that piece is read backwards
only a piece of the words meat cat nibbled is taken

explanation.surface: A cat has gnawed round a chunk of meat but left it whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of' takes TCATNI from 'meaT CAT NIbbled'; 'around' turns it back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Intact means undamaged and complete.

clue.text: Store in foreign country delivered to some

indicators.note: spoken, as some speakers would deliver it, dropping the r

parts.note: Ghana is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: Goods held in storage abroad and shipped to a few customers.
explanation.walkthrough: In an accent that drops the R, GHANA and GARNER sound the same; 'to some' admits that not every speaker says them alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To garner is to gather and lay up, as grain in a granary.

clue.text: Host's crackers to appear topless

indicators.note: without its top, so the first letter of the word for crackers is dropped

parts.note: crackers and barmy both mean mad

explanation.surface: A party host goes mad and appears without a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the B from BARMY.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a great multitude, especially an armed one, as in 'a heavenly host'.

clue.text: Drops retired cook as public relations expert

indicators.note: retiring is going back, so the word for drops is read backwards

parts.note: nips are small drops of spirits
to cook the books is to doctor them, falsify

explanation.surface: A retired chef takes his medicine in drops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns NIPS into SPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor is a press agent who puts a favourable slant on news for a politician or party.

clue.text: Opening remark that defends union taking time off

indicators.note: the remark surrounds and so guards the other piece

parts.note: a comment is a remark

indicators.note: time is taken off, removed

parts.note: cement binds and unites, a union

explanation.surface: An opening speech that defends a trade union taking time off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is just a link; 'off' does the removing, and cement counts as a union because it binds things together.
explanation.definitionFit: A commencement is a beginning or start.

clue.text: Consistency in sharing money, but not to burn

indicators.note: says the letters for burning are removed from the phrase sharing money

parts.note: to singe is to burn lightly

explanation.surface: A householder shares the money but refuses to set any of it alight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes S, I, N, G and E, scattered in order, from SHARINGMONEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmony is agreement or accord among parts, a sense of consistency.

clue.text: Solid, three-dimensional, large empty compartment

parts.note: cubic describes a solid, three-dimensional shape

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its shell, so just the outer letters of large are used

explanation.surface: A description of a big, boxy, empty storage space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves LE from 'large'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubicle is a small partitioned space, such as a changing booth.

clue.text: Greek food obtained from Turk, most loth to receive American replacements regularly

indicators.note: A stands for American, and regularly, at every second position, the words take that letter in place of their own

explanation.surface: A reluctant Turk has to accept American substitutes at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep T, R, M, S, L, T from 'Turk, most loth' and put A (American) in place of each alternate letter U, K, O, T, O, H, giving TaRaMaSaLaTa.
explanation.definitionFit: Taramasalata is a pink Greek dip made from fish roe.

clue.text: Government minister creates confusion over railway

indicators.note: confusion signals that the letters of creates are mixed up

explanation.surface: A minister causes chaos over rail policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion' gives SECRETA; 'over' puts it above RY in this down entry. In Britain senior ministers are Secretaries of State.
explanation.definitionFit: A Secretary of State heads a UK government department.

clue.text: Kiss model, so cute outside Californian location

indicators.note: the reshaped letters sit outside the city
to model is to shape, so the letters of so cute are reshaped

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, in California

explanation.surface: A cute model is kissed outside a Los Angeles venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' gives OSCUTE, which goes around LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Osculate is a formal or jocular verb for kissing.

clue.text: Putting together part of school timetable

definitions.meaning: fitting parts into a whole, as with flat-pack furniture
the morning gathering of pupils and staff in a school hall

explanation.definitionFit: Assembly is construction from parts, and also a gathering of a whole school.

clue.text: Those who may seem old-fashioned if abusing chairman's son

indicators.note: abusing means misusing, so the letters are mistreated into a new order

explanation.surface: An outdated attitude is exposed when a chairman mistreats his son.
explanation.definitionFit: Anachronisms are things out of their proper time, like outdated relics.

clue.text: Capricorn is one theme absorbing astrologer ultimately

indicators.note: the theme takes in the letter

parts.note: a topic is a theme

indicators.note: the ultimate, final letter of astrologer

explanation.surface: An astrologer's theme of the day is the star sign Capricorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capricorn' points at the zodiac, but it is the Tropic of Capricorn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tropic of Capricorn is a line of latitude south of the equator.

clue.text: Outline content of newspaper cutbacks

indicators.note: the contents held inside the words newspaper cutbacks

explanation.surface: A summary of the content of a newspaper's cost cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperçu is a brief summary or insight.

clue.text: Full summer in France after hesitation over coming to Poland

indicators.note: turned over, so the hesitation sound is written backwards

parts.note: er is the sound of a speaker hesitating
PL is the international code for Poland
été is French for summer

explanation.surface: A traveller, full after a French summer, hesitates before moving on to Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' and 'coming to' only set the order, so the French summer goes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means filled to capacity, especially well fed.

clue.text: Corrupt vote starts to unsettle troubled electorate

parts.note: a poll is a vote

indicators.note: the starts, the opening letters, of the next three words

explanation.surface: A rigged ballot begins to disturb an already worried electorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To pollute is to contaminate or debase, a figurative corruption.

clue.text: Animal's sire carrying recessive genetic footprint

indicators.note: the father's word holds the other piece

parts.note: a sire is a father, pa

indicators.note: receding, going back, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: DNA is the genetic fingerprint

explanation.surface: An animal's father passes on a recessive genetic trait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recessive' turns DNA into AND, which PA carries; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is a black-and-white bear of China.

clue.text: Various ceramics on special offer finally gone

indicators.note: gone in the sense of crazy, so the letters are scrambled
the final letter of offer

explanation.surface: A shop's assorted pottery was on promotion and has now sold out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' rearranges ONSPECIAL plus R; 'Various' marks the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelains are fine china wares, a plural for several kinds of fired pottery.

clue.text: Old actress removing old dress

indicators.note: taking away a letter from the actress's name

parts.note: Greta Garbo was a film star of the 1920s and 30s

explanation.surface: A veteran actress takes off her old frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' takes O from GARBO.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, an old-fashioned word for attire.

clue.text: Reckon stationer must be a rural chap

parts.note: to count is to reckon or calculate
Ryman is a British chain of stationery shops

explanation.surface: Someone judges that a stationery seller must be a country bumpkin.
explanation.walkthrough: RYMAN is a high-street stationery chain in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A countryman is a man who lives in the countryside.

clue.text: Challenge Fury at last after having provided what's necessary for comeback

indicators.note: a comeback goes back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to have fed someone is to have supplied what they need

indicators.note: at last means at the very end, so only the closing letter of Fury is wanted

explanation.surface: A boxer named Fury challenges a rival after preparing properly for a return bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for comeback' makes DEF of FED; Tyson Fury is a British heavyweight boxer, which suits 'comeback'.
explanation.definitionFit: To defy is to resist openly, to challenge authority.
